exposure: Phase of labour at hospital admission (latent phase vs. active phase)
outcome: Maternal outcomes (perineal tears, cervical tears, PPH, retained placenta, augmentation, caesarean section for dystocia, instrumental delivery, third stage complications)
Neonatal outcomes (APGAR scores, NICU admission, neonatal complications)
cohort: The study included 300 low-risk primigravid women (200 in latent phase admission group, 100 in active phase admission group) admitted to the Department of Obstetrics & Gynecology, Murshidabad Medical college and Hospital.
finding: Early admission to the hospital during the latent phase of labour in low-risk women is associated with a significantly increased risk of perineal tears, early initiation of augmentation, increased rates of caesarean section for dystocia, increased instrumental delivery, and increased third stage complications compared to admission during the active phase.
mod_finding: Admission during the latent phase of labour was associated with an increased rate of caesarean section for dystocia and instrumental delivery.
